en:
"Desperation is the song of the destitute, and our song echoes from the towering spires to the crypts below. We are the lowest. We, who grasp at the straws of betterment, prostrated before the great tunnels of the gods, aching for another sip of divinity. Our homes, our toil, and our world—all lie within the cold stone."

- Chiselled in stone, unknown author

"In times of wealth and prosperity, few thoughts linger on proclamations of ruination, and scarce are those not enthralled by the splendor of dyes, the smell of exotic spices, and the wondrous glimmer of Ichor.

We failed our gods. During the First Emergence, when the crimson Light caressed our Grand Bazaar, we did not perceive It as an omen. We did not foresee the calamity soon to follow. The gods were no more, and the very lifeblood of our Bazaar, our currency most dear, was lost with them."

- Endus, the repentant

"The warmth of the Gardens sends shivers through my delighted flesh. I rose from the vats, scaled the plateaus, frolicked in the grass, and lazed beneath the trees. I ate, and ate, and ate. The Gardens were left to wilt, and so have become my domain.

It is inevitable now. I still hear the chanting as the dead were poured into the vats. The sizzling and bubbling. Mouth-watering vapors. My beloved Gardens, now more alive than anything remaining in this City of stone."

- Achretis

"The murals tell of a time before the ice—a time of vast waters brimming with strange life, from whence the Progenitors once crawled. What a sight it must have been, to behold the birth of gods.

Malformed and wondrous, their blessed forms held the miracles we now take for granted, ushering in an age of prosperity for all.

Yet no age lasts eternally. The Emergence of the Red Star wrought calamity upon our world. Cast down from the heights above, we now linger in the dark tunnels carved by our long-lost gods."

- Belgurum the Scholar

"Basked in the Red Star's Light across innumerable centuries, the Observatory remains the sole structure able to reach beyond the ice. Once a beacon of prosperity, it now stands as a derelict testament to the technological achievements of our distant past.

From it, the Sisters and their following watched the black sky, staring into the darkness between the stars. In the emptiness, something stirred, and like minds took notice.

Within the Observatory, they tore open the first Gate, artificing wonders that sang in tune to the Void. Yet such careless exposure does not come without risk, and beings not native to our world have since overtaken its umbral halls."

- So-Venat, the channeler

"Subtle are the signs of the Chroniclers and endless is their Repository, hidden within the folds of time and space. A creature never before seen; a growth that springs from nowhere; a disease without origin. As wielders of the Void and masters of the Gate, their reach remains immeasurably wide.

We call them Chroniclers, for they have never named themselves. Gifts, threats, sacrifices, and song—they ignore all but that which interferes with their work, which is to chronicle every speck of dust, every vibration in the air, every surface struck by light, and every strand of time."

- Time-lost scholar

"I alone created this glimpse into our past. Pity me that I cannot move beyond its splendor, despite how pale it appears in comparison. Through my mirrors I behold the world outside, lifeless and devoid of color. It saddens me. Everything turns to dust; such is the way of things. But, by my hand alone, a speck of what was lost may be reclaimed."

- The Vizier

"What does it mean to touch the very womb of creation? I journeyed far into the darkness in pursuit of it, but no recount could have prepared me for its visage. Its iridescent nacre shell shimmered in all the colors of the world, caressed by dark veins traveling far into the ruins above.

Around me danced strands of glowing light, which I recognized as the blessed liquid so divine. This, I thought, must be where the blood of the gods journeyed upon death. Awestruck, I lingered. Words cannot convey the sensation of its touch, nor the majesty of listening to the unworldly reverberations of the heartbeat of a god."

- Unknown author

"How does one begin to fathom the space between all worlds? The counterbalance to the known, the endless expanse bordering the real, Its vast nothingness lingers on in perpetuity, unchanged. Yet within lay the key to our ascension, or so we believed. Guided by unseen hands, we pursued salvation from the trappings of our mortal shells. How foolish we were.

The Void is not for us, for it is our opposite—a realm of the unrealized and unmade, a cage for whispering dead gods. While our great achievements allowed us to channel some of its flows for our benefit, only those not of our world may truly pass beyond its dark veil."

- Yantir the Apostate
Notes on the Void

I will never reveal my name.

The priests, the nobles, and the scholars—they are all mistaken. Lost in ignorance. The Void is not a mere bridge between worlds.

All things can be categorized, and all things fall onto a spectrum of energy, a scale inherently balancing itself. That is its function. It is not a petty means of translocation, nor merely a material to be utilized.

It is the manifestation of entropy—the force that balances, and the end that reclaims all.
Study of the Mutilants

One-month vigil. The stellar phenomenon was calm. No loss.

Two-month vigil. A stellar abnormality. Pulses from the dark. Two dead. The blessed within the black obelisk seem invigorated. Screams were heard from beyond the obsidian wall.

Three-month vigil. Sounds from the dark. The blessed are thriving. They do not wander. Ecstatic dances. Surge from the Star. More adaptation. The blessed now have neither arms nor legs. Their bodies move through the air.
The Rods

The accursed rods. We stole them. Held them. Tried to understand. We don't disobey, yet they pierce our flesh.

They had much, and we were hungry. Why can't we just eat?

Two were caught. Now they don't see us anymore. They stare and wait. They don't look to be in pain.

I don't sleep anymore. The metal plays in my mind. Maybe I, too, could be taken. Maybe I, too, could live without hunger and pain.
What grows in the Gardens

Seed. Sprout. Growth. Wither. Death. Rot. 

The alchemists speak in the dark. They are not like the learned of the Observatory, but peddlers of sorcery. The air itself hisses upon their touch.

Our granaries no longer hold any seeds. Nothing sprouts as it should in the Gardens. It just is. Through the Salt they speak things into being, housing it within their offal jars.

These rituals frighten me.
What lies beyond

I am old now. My eyes grow gray, yet I have come to see. To understand.

Our libraries are vast, the volumes within telling of a world outside of the City. I have read them all. Tomes and scrolls reveal to us other nations, sprouting cities, and cultures scattered across this world.

It is only once you have read all, as I have, that you begin to notice the discordant notes within the melody, the colors of thread clashing within the tapestry. Inconsistencies, implausibilities, and fabrications. Then there remains but one question for the honest scholar to pose. Is it all a lie?

Yes. I propose that we are entirely alone. Never has there been anyone beyond the vast oceans, beyond the archipelago. Beyond the City, there is no one else, and there never was.
Uut the Screamer lies!

The fool shouts and screams. His voice is shrill, his words unkind, hysterical, and devious. He screams without end, and every word is a lie.

I hate him. I hate him. I hate him.

Why do so many listen? Fill his mouth with dirt and throw him into the offal vats where he belongs. Why do they listen? He is loud. He does not soothe, help, or enlighten. He merely screams without end.
Reflections

She left us. The others think it is because she longed for the past, unable to let it go. Fools.

She left because, despite our efforts, we did not gain understanding. Not like her or her Sister.

We looked to tame the Void, and we did. We found uses for its energies. We understood how to manipulate it, to artifice, and to create.

I now realize that the mirrors are not just nostalgic monuments. They are the only way to truly gaze into the Void, to learn what it has to teach. A reflection of what we truly know. A reflection of nothing.
The visitor

It didn’t say anything, my beloved lord.

We gave it gold in an attempt at good faith, to try to make it speak. Pushing all others aside, it proceeded to study a single coin. For three days, it fixated on that one coin—then abruptly put it down, all interest lost. As you instructed, we waited a fortnight to see if we could regain its notice, yet it remained still.

When we hurt it—gods, the things we did to it—it never showed any sign of pain. At least, not in the sense you or I could discern.

Even when we severed its stalk-like head, its faceted features seemed not to convey fright, but merely an unsettling curiosity.
Every stone

The scale of our City is grander than any tales could do justice.

Once, I lived in the Commons. It was my whole world. The movement of life through its perpetual stone halls was like watching a stream winding its way through a pebbled riverbed.

Still, a river is nothing compared to the ocean, and how could I remain in one place alone? I walked for days through stone and dirt, seeing spires rise and listening to the chanting of a thousand faiths. Endless is our great City, and I shall walk its every stone.
Crude petroglyph

I awoke in the ice long ago. Before water. Before cities. Before light. Here I lay, for so long I thought it impossible to ever stir.

Torn from the whole. I moved my limbs, I dug. Deeper, further. I didn’t know what I was, yet I began to sense.

Piercing sounds of tiny movements. Forms of life, floating in the water. I smelled vibrations in the air as energies played in different fluctuations.

The entirety of existence moves. I must be a god.
The divine

I always thought the gods would be beautiful—divine beings to gaze at in awe, as the old stories said.

Perhaps I am but a fool, unable to comprehend what it means to be divine. It is not beauty as I understand it. I pray daily, as all should, yet I feel naught but horror and disgust when I behold them.

I must be a fool, for we all thrive by their holy blessings.
Faith is a gift

Faith, dearest flock, is a gift in its own right. It is the banishment of worry, doubt, and erratic aims.

Yet, despite the blessings bestowed upon us by the gods, there are still those who oppose our faith—misguided souls fit only to serve as sustenance for the great vats. To the devout, faith promises beauty in existence and purpose in death.

Bare your teeth, dearest flock, for the gods have seen fit to bless us with their Flesh so supple. Eat well and drink deep of their nectar ever-flowing, for through it, we hear their voices. I ask you, how can those deaf to their wonders ever ascend to a greater purpose?
The Cradle

We dug for days at the behest of the stonemasons, mining the winding veins of dark metal running through the stone far below the great foundations. We toiled without end, the tunnels shimmering with mesmerizing metal dust.

A messenger arrived from the tunnels below. Something in her eyes... I've never seen the like of it. All were called into the depths.

I could scarcely believe my eyes when I knelt among the others before its nacre shell. It rested silently within the stone, caressed by the very metal we mined. Ichor, reshaping itself. I will never count myself among the learned, but even one such as I can recognize the presence of the gods.
The navigator

When It called out across the waters, I was the first to listen. They did not yet see, so I brought us beneath Its light.

Much was found, much was brought, and the metal sang.

When first I held the voice of the divine within my palm, cold and dark... Disgust overcame me. I saw the putridity of my form. And I wept.

The flesh must first rot away, cast off like a beggar's tatters, before one can be born anew.
The holy mycelium
